name: Learn to crochet
blurb: One hook, one live stitch, and mistakes that pull out cleanly. Crochet is faster to learn than knitting and much easier to undo, which makes it the friendlier starting point.
steps: Learn the slip knot, the chain, and how to count chains — miscounting the foundation chain is the classic first frustration.
Learn the single crochet (UK double), working into the back bump of the chain for a tidy edge.
Learn the double crochet (UK treble) and the difference the turning chain makes.
Learn to work in the round to make a granny square, which introduces working into spaces rather than stitches.
Learn to read a simple pattern and its abbreviations, checking whether it is UK or US terminology.
Make several squares and join them into something real.
tips: UK and US stitch names differ and mean different stitches. Check which a pattern uses before starting.
Losing or gaining stitches at the ends is nearly always the turning chain. Count every row.
proof: A finished blanket square or small bag, with straight sides and a consistent stitch count.
